# MTRClust

MTRClust is an R package for robust clustering of multivariate panel
trajectories. The method fits smooth low-rank cluster trajectories, trims whole
observations, and records multilevel outlier diagnostics for complete numeric
panel arrays.

The main input is a numeric three-dimensional array with dimensions
`n x T x p`, where `n` is the number of units, `T` is the number of ordered time
points, and `p` is the number of variables or sensors.

## Features

- Robust clustering of complete multivariate panel arrays.
- Observation-level trimming through `alpha`.
- Smooth low-rank fitted cluster trajectories.
- Explicit termination, convergence, and rollback diagnostics.
- Observation, temporal, sensor-segment, multivariate-segment, and cell-level
  diagnostic summaries.
- S3 `print()`, `summary()`, and `plot()` methods.
- Small synthetic data generator and long-format-to-array helper.

## Installation

From a local source package:

```r
install.packages("MTRClust_0.1.0.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

From GitHub after the public repository has been created:

```r
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("hsnbulut/MTRClust")
```

Repository target: <https://github.com/hsnbulut/MTRClust>

## Minimum example

```{r example}
library(MTRClust)

dat <- simulate_mtr_panel(n = 30, tt = 15, p = 3, seed = 1)
fit <- mtrclust(
  x = dat$x,
  k = 3,
  alpha = 0.05,
  rank = 2,
  nstart = 2,
  max_iter = 20,
  seed = 1
)

fit
summary(fit)
plot(fit, type = "objective")
```

This example was run during package-release preparation. It converged without
rollback using `max_iter = 20` on the synthetic data generated above.

## Diagnostics

```{r diagnostics}
mtrclust_diagnostics(fit)
head(mtrclust_diagnostics(fit, type = "units"))
```

Use the help pages and introductory vignette for the full argument list and
interpretation details:

```r
?mtrclust
vignette("introduction-to-mtrclust", package = "MTRClust")
```

## Reproducibility

`mtrclust()` uses sequential random starts by default. Set `seed` explicitly to
make the stochastic initialization reproducible. The returned object records the
main user arguments, termination reason, convergence flag, rollback flag,
iteration count, best iteration, objective value, and diagnostic summaries.

## Limitations

The current wrapper requires complete finite numeric arrays. Missing values are
not imputed. The default execution path is sequential. Termination by
`max_iter` is reported separately from convergence, and rollback to the best
objective iterate is explicitly recorded.

## Citation

If you use MTRClust in research, please cite the accompanying MTRClust methods
article. The article DOI is not available yet and should not be invented. The
package citation can be inspected with:

```r
citation("MTRClust")
```

No separate software DOI is planned for this package.

## Development status

Version `0.1.0` is the initial public source release prepared for GitHub
publication. The scientific implementation follows the audited prototype used
in the accompanying methods manuscript. The public API uses `method = "global"`
by default; the legacy internal alias `"v6_global"` remains accepted for
reproducibility.
